stem:
Myra compares a water clock, a sundial, a candle clock, and an hourglass.

Which claim correctly matches a device to the observable change it uses to mark time?

options.text: A water clock uses water flowing from one vessel to another.
A sundial uses a shadow that keeps marking time at night with no sunlight.
A candle clock uses only the flame getting dimmer.
An hourglass uses water flowing from its upper bulb to its lower bulb.

teacher.key_rationale: A water clock marks time by water flow. A sundial needs sunlight for its shadow; a candle clock uses marked burning, not only a dimmer flame; an hourglass uses sand, not water.
